title: Anthropic's Scion is heavily inspired by Mononoke

comments.comment:
I read this post and was angry on the author's behalf. Then I learned - not from the post - that in fact one of the things Anthropic did credit is the larger system of which Mononoke is a component. This has made me much less upset with Anthropic and moderately upset with this post's author for not stating this up front. I'm willing to believe that this was omitted only because it's hard to remember that these things aren't background knowledge to everyone, rather than e.g. to make this seem like a bigger deal to readers than it would otherwise (which is the effect this omission had on me), but I think this post ought to be clearer about that.

With this context, and having re-read Anthropic's post, I don't think Anthropic behaved badly here, unless there's even more context I'm still missing. Can someone who is upset even with this context spell out in a little more detail what you think the problem is?

Two years ago, adopting an open source system and helping improve it may have been the best option.

This year, with unlimited Claude credits, I would likely have made the same decision they did. Contributing to an existing project is a lot more time consuming than building from scratch (thanks to the human coordination overhead), and time is the only resource they didn't have in abundance.

You don't have to carry their water in every post.

I don't.

comments.comment:
Thanks.

FYI in your post you say:

it looks like the core concept of "derived data" was heavily inspired by Mononoke, the server component of Sapling

I want to be clear that it isn't just the concept of derived data that is inspired by Mononoke. A Scion changeset is almost exactly the same as what we in Mononoke called a Bonsai changeset. I led the design and initial implementation work for Bonsai changesets back in 2018, including writing the four canonical design documents that are still the reference. The advantages of Bonsai changesets are very non-obvious until you spend a great deal of time thinking about the problem, which I had given my years of experience on version control.

This is not surprising given the additional information I received later, which includes the fact that Claude was pointed directly at Mononoke and told to copy it. The fact that none of this is even remotely hinted at is shameful; taking an existing battle-tested (over a decade!) design and copying it in 5 months is much less impressive than coming up with a brand new design and productionizing it in 5 months.

edit to add that there are also other parts such as an API to do source control queries and mutations with that are copied from Mononoke. Those have been done elsewhere before Mononoke, too. In general it is always good to situate your work in the larger context of what came before you.
